title: finding(components,app-shell,plugin-gantt,plugin-calendar): four more date faces hand the UI language to a formatter instead of `useDisplayLocale()`: data-table date cells, record audit history, the gantt resource workload and the calendar default locale
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a product defect with named sites, read at source. Reader: triage first (route and grade), then the execution seat that claims it.

Filed by the `domain:ui#4` execution seat (`session_01BP8CMtACxTdLjqR6rhd33C`) at the ACCEPT of objectui#10375 (PR objectui#10431). The contract review of that PR found these sites. ⛔ Filed bare, not graded here.

## The defect

The display-locale contract in `packages/i18n/src/useDisplayLocale.ts` says: "Every date, number and currency renderer goes through here." objectui#10331 and objectui#10375 moved five faces onto it. Four more date faces still format with the translation hook's UI `language`. They pass it as a helper's `locale` option or through a local variable, not as a direct `toLocale*` first argument, so the objectui#9909 census cannot see them. Read on objectui `origin/main`:

| site | how the UI language reaches the formatter |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx` | date cells call `formatDateTime(value, { locale: language })` and `formatDate(value, undefined, { locale: language })`, with `language` from `useTableTranslation()`. core's `DateDisplayOptions.locale` is documented as the BCP-47 display locale |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` | audit history builds `fmtCtx = { t, locale: language, lookupLabels }`, and `formatScalar` in `auditHistoryDisplay.ts` spends it on `toLocaleDateString` / `toLocaleString` |
| `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ResourceWorkload.tsx` | `const locale = language || undefined`, then `toLocaleDateString(locale, …)`. An empty language also falls through to the machine locale |
| `packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx` | `effectiveLocale = locale !== "default" ? locale : language`, where the `locale` prop defaults to `"default"` |

The effect is the one measured on objectui#10331 and objectui#10375. With an English UI and a `de-CH` display locale, a date renders `3/4/2020` instead of `4.3.2020`: readable, but in an order that goes against the user's setting.

Not in scope: the reviewer checked the other `locale: language` hits (`RecordDetailView` action params, `useConsoleActionRuntime`, `FlowRunner`, `usePackageL10n`). They choose per-locale LABEL maps, which is a translation choice, not a formatter.

## Evidence

Read at source by the objectui#10431 reviewer. The seat re-read the data-table, `RecordDetailView` and `ResourceWorkload` lines on `origin/main`. ⛔ Not probed in a render.

## Grading notes (for triage, not a grade)

- The same class and grade as objectui#10331 and objectui#10375 (p3). The fix shape is theirs: read `useDisplayLocale()` in the component, with ⛔ no fallback, and pass it where `language` goes today. Pin each face with an English UI and a `de-CH` display locale.
- The sites span four packages. Triage may split them or keep one card.
- A census name rule would not catch these either (they are helper options, not direct first arguments). That is one reason per-surface pins are the reliable check here.

## Dedupe

REST page walk over the 1000 most recently updated objectui items. The pattern `data-table` near locale / language, `ResourceWorkload` near locale / language, `CalendarView` near `effectiveLocale` / display locale / language, `auditHistoryDisplay`, or `fmtCtx` ⇒ 2 hits. One is objectui#10183 (closed; renderers pre-parsing date strings, a different defect). The other is objectui#10144 (closed; the calendar month gridcell's runtime-default name, a different site). The control `useDisplayLocale` ⇒ 10 hits, among them objectui#10375 and objectui#10331, so the instrument is lit.

Dedupe words: `data-table formatDateTime locale language` · `audit history fmtCtx locale language` · `ResourceWorkload toLocaleDateString language` · `CalendarView effectiveLocale default language` · `display locale helper option`
